app.title: Ankle fracture classification
app.description: Answer the questions to obtain the Lauge-Hansen, Danis-Weber, AO/OTA, and Bartonicek classification

hero.title: Four ankle fracture classifications from one set of answers.
hero.lede: Anklyze is an open-source tool for classifying ankle fractures. It follows a single decision tree: answer what you see on the radiograph and it returns the Lauge-Hansen, Danis-Weber, AO/OTA and Bartonicek classifications together.

example.caption: Example: an isolated lateral malleolus fracture, read through the tree. N/C means the system does not apply.

method.title: Method
method.tableLink: See every path of the decision tree

tree.body: Every question belongs to a single tree with 165 terminal paths. Each answer decides the next question, and each path ends in a classification in all four systems. The tree is published in the repository as a diagram and as a table.

tested.body: The classification engine's tests are generated from the same diagram as the tree. They currently cover 88 of the 165 paths; the rest are not yet tested automatically.

notClassifiable.body: When a system does not apply to the fracture, the result says so (N/C) instead of forcing a code.

judgement.term: It does not replace clinical judgement
judgement.body: Anklyze makes the reasoning explicit and keeps the path that led to each result. The decision remains the surgeon's; always correlate with the clinical findings.

systems.title: The four systems
systems.lede: Each system describes the same fracture from a different angle. Anklyze reports them side by side, so none has to be worked out separately.
systems.laugeHansen: Mechanism of injury: the position of the foot and the direction of the deforming force.
systems.danisWeber: Level of the fibular fracture relative to the syndesmosis.
systems.aoota: Alphanumeric code for bone, segment, type and group.
systems.bartonicek: Morphology of the posterior malleolus fragment.

studies.title: Research use
studies.lede: The same classifier is used to run inter-rater reliability studies: researchers publish cases with their imaging, raters classify them independently, and the application reports how far they agree.

cases.body: Radiographs and CT for one fracture, classified by each rater without seeing the others.

agreement.body: Kappa for each classification system, with its Landis and Koch interpretation.

gold.body: Each rater's accuracy against the reference classification set by the study.

footer.disclaimer: For medical purposes only. Always correlate with clinical findings.
footer.license: Code: Apache 2.0. Decision tree: CC BY 4.0

source.title: Open source
source.body: The code, the decision tree and the statistical methodology are public. The code is free software under the Apache 2.0 licence; the decision tree is under CC BY 4.0 and can be reused with credit to its author.

The four classification systems belong to their original authors; Anklyze is not affiliated with the AO Foundation or the Orthopaedic Trauma Association.

method.title: Method
method.fleissRaters: Fleiss' kappa is computed over the raters who answered every case; at least two such raters are needed. Raters included: {{raters}} of {{totalRaters}}. Cases: {{cases}}.
method.interval: The {{level}}% interval for Fleiss' kappa is a percentile bootstrap: the cases are resampled with replacement 2000 times with a fixed seed, so the same data always gives the same interval. Resamples in which every rating falls in one category have no kappa and are skipped. The interval is limited to the range −1 to 1. A wide interval means the estimate is uncertain.
method.labels: Interpretation labels follow Landis and Koch (1977).
method.percentAgreement: Each figure is the share of responses that match the most common classification for this case, computed for each system over the responses that have a classification in that system. A single response counts as 100%. Responses: {{responses}}. Raters: {{raters}}.
method.fleissCases: For each system, only the cases that all of those raters answered in that system are used. A case where a rater gave no answer in a system is left out of that system and counted as excluded. A system needs at least two usable cases.
method.cohen: When exactly two raters answered every case, Cohen's kappa is shown too, computed across the cases both answered in that system. Its {{level}}% interval is a normal approximation, kappa ± z·SE with SE = √(Po·(1−Po) / (N·(1−Pe)²)), limited to the range −1 to 1. It has no width when Po is 0 or 1.
method.weighted: AO/OTA weighted kappa uses linear weights over the order 44-A1, A2, A3, B1, B2, B3, C1, C2, C3. Subgroup codes are compared by their group (44-B1.2 counts as 44-B1). A pair with a code outside that order, such as 43-B1 or not classifiable, is left out and counted.
method.noKappaPerCase: Kappa is not computed for a single case: one case gives each rater one rating, so kappa could only be 1 or 0. Kappa is reported per study.

reliability.weightedUnavailable: AO/OTA weighted kappa is not available: fewer than two pairs of ratings have both codes in the AO/OTA order.
